objective: Let a gate declare the input closure that owns its verdict, so stale evidence is admissible only when nothing in that closure moved.
falsifiable_claim: The claim fails if a change inside a gate's declared input closure leaves that gate's prior evidence admissible, or if a declared closure omits an input that demonstrably moves the verdict.
in_scope: Per-gate declared input closures as pinned literal data.
Mechanically enforced self-inclusion: a closure covers its own verifier and producers.
An end-to-end acceptance harness that mutates a real input and requires stale evidence to be refused.
out_of_scope: Debuting the control inside another cut's closing round. It debuts under its own review or not at all.
Any proof runner that reports failure without a nonzero exit code.

aggregate_disposition.why: Withdrawn from the M5 event-substrate cut by owner ruling on Codex option (b) 2026-08-04. The mechanism was sound in intent and defective in execution, and a control must not become load-bearing for a packet it was written inside. It debuts under its own review.

implementation_actions: Re-derive closures from measured verdict-ownership rather than assumption.
Give every proof runner a nonzero exit on failure and prove it by inverting a proof.
Add the end-to-end mutation harness before any closure is trusted.
positive_proof: A change inside a declared closure refuses the prior evidence, proven end-to-end by mutating a real input and re-running the gate.
A declared closure covers its own verifier and producers, checked mechanically rather than asserted.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: CODEX ATTACK 1, VERBATIM: an INVERTED proof runner -- one whose assertions all fail -- must exit NONZERO. The withdrawn runner printed PASS/FAIL lines and never set an exit code, so its 7/7 was structurally unfalsifiable by exit status and its presence in the gate list made a green packet independent of whether the proofs held.

CODEX ATTACK 2, VERBATIM: an end-to-end mutation under third_party/ must invalidate stale Rust-gate evidence. A closure that omits a real input is itself a label asserting a closure nobody computed -- the failure mode the mechanism existed to prevent, reproduced inside the mechanism.
remaining_nonclaims: This record does not claim the withdrawn implementation was correct in any part beyond its intent.
This record does not claim declared closures are the only way to make stale evidence safe.
rollback_or_stop_rule: Stop if a closure cannot be derived from measured verdict-ownership; an assumed closure is the defect, not the mechanism.
current_implementation_evidence: FILED 2026-08-04 on owner ruling, Codex option (b). The declared-input-surface mechanism built during the M5 event-substrate closing round is WITHDRAWN from that cut entirely so the literal depends on substrate plus pin fix plus the strict measured-commit rule and nothing else. Two P0 defects found by Codex are recorded above as this record's acceptance tests. The process lesson is recorded with them: a control labelled non-load-bearing whose PROOF SUITE sits in the gate list is load-bearing for the packet's green, because the packet passes only if that suite exits zero -- and that suite always exited zero. Not-load-bearing is a property of the wiring, not of the label.
